controls.name: Uniform retraining of baselines
controls.detail: Re-implement or use official code to retrain all compared methods on the same training data/splits and preprocessing.
controls.rules_out: Performance differences arising from disparate training data, preprocessing, or initialization rather than the proposed intervention.

Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

controls.name: No-augmentation baseline and leave-one-out
controls.detail: Train the same model with no data augmentations and with all-but-one augmentations.
controls.rules_out: Gains attributable purely to augmentation pipelines instead of the proposed method.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection

controls.name: Backbone and pretraining swaps
controls.detail: Hold the pipeline fixed while changing backbones (e.g., ResNet/EfficientNet/Xception) and toggling ImageNet pretraining.
controls.rules_out: Improvements driven by backbone choice or pretraining rather than the proposed component.
evidence: DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

controls.name: Quality-level training variants
controls.detail: Train on FF++ Raw, c23, c40, and combined to test dependence on training compression level.
controls.rules_out: Apparent robustness due only to matching training compression to test conditions.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations

controls.name: Uncompressed test baseline
controls.detail: Evaluate on pristine test data alongside distorted sets.
controls.rules_out: Robustness gains that come at the cost of clean-data accuracy.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations

controls.name: Single-model vs ensemble and fusion ablations
controls.detail: Report single-model performance and compare fusion strategies (majority vote, probability averaging, logit averaging).

Process-Driven Modelling of Media Forensic Investigations-Considerations on the Example of DeepFake Detection

controls.name: Inference-resolution and TTA ablations
controls.detail: Use the same checkpoint at different input resolutions and switch TTA (e.g., flips) on/off.
controls.rules_out: Apparent improvements caused by resolution scaling or test-time tricks rather than model design.
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild

controls.name: Within-domain-only vs cross-domain-only augmentation
controls.detail: Train with only within-domain augmentations and only cross-domain mixup in isolation.
controls.rules_out: Attribution of gains to one augmentation family when the other is responsible.
evidence: Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

controls.name: Component ablations for adapters
controls.detail: Remove individual adapter components (e.g., GBA-only, LSA-only) versus full adapter.
controls.rules_out: That a single submodule explains the full gain.
evidence: DeepFake-Adapter: Dual-Level Adapter for DeepFake Detection

controls.name: Temporal modeling ablation
controls.detail: Compare ViT-only frame classifier to ViT + temporal transformer; evaluate with and without smoothing.
controls.rules_out: Gains from temporal IoU/AUC caused by image encoder or post-hoc smoothing rather than temporal modeling.
evidence: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos

controls.name: Chance (guessing) baseline
controls.detail: Include a random/guessing baseline or report kappa vs chance.
controls.rules_out: Detectors performing at chance level being mistaken for effective.
evidence: Process-Driven Modelling of Media Forensic Investigations-Considerations on the Example of DeepFake Detection

controls.name: Human-perception-vetted hard set
controls.detail: Construct a hard test subset by retaining fakes judged real by humans in a blind study.
controls.rules_out: Evaluation hardness due to trivially visible artifacts rather than imperceptible forgeries.
evidence: Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

confounds.detail: Differences in dataset versions, compression levels, face alignment, or train/test splits can inflate or deflate reported performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run all methods in a unified benchmark with identical preprocessing, splits, and hyperparameters (e.g., DeepfakeBench) and/or retrain baselines uniformly.

Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Overfitting to dataset/manipulation-specific artifacts
confounds.detail: A model may perform well in-domain but fail on unseen datasets or manipulation types.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Cross-dataset tests (e.g., train FF++, test Celeb-DF/DFDC/DFD/DF1.0/WDF) and cross-manipulation evaluations within FF++.

confounds.name: Gains due to augmentation choices or added synthetic data
confounds.detail: Performance may improve from specific augmentations or extra synthetic data coverage rather than the proposed algorithm.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablations with/without augmentations, leave-one-out augmentation analyses, and retraining baselines on the same augmented data.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection

confounds.name: Reliance on pixel-level/blending cues not robust to perturbations
confounds.detail: Detectors may latch onto fragile low-level artifacts that vanish under distortions or new generators.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Robustness sweeps over blur/JPEG/noise/contrast/saturation and tests on GAN/diffusion-generated images; report per-distortion and average AUC.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Backbone/pretraining/ensembling or TTA explains improvements
confounds.detail: Observed gains might stem from stronger backbones, pretraining, ensembling, or test-time tricks.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Backbone/pretraining swaps, single-model vs ensemble reports, fusion-strategy ablations, and TTA/resolution ablations.
evidence: DeepFake-Adapter: Dual-Level Adapter for DeepFake Detection
DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Visual quality distribution differences drive performance
confounds.detail: Quality mismatches between real and fake (or between splits) may act as spurious cues.

confounds.name: Clean-only evaluation inflates results (lack of robustness)
confounds.detail: High scores on pristine data may not hold under common distortions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate across multiple distortion types and severities and average AUC across them.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Implementation/reimplementation errors
confounds.detail: Discrepancies could be due to coding mistakes rather than true method differences.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Verify re-implementations against original reported results or use official code/weights where possible.
evidence: Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Fusion operator artifacts
confounds.detail: Performance differences could arise from a particular fusion rule rather than the added detectors/models.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare multiple fusion operators (e.g., majority, probability, logit averaging) and report consistent trends.
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild

confounds.name: Unstable rankings due to single random perturbation/severity
confounds.detail: Applying a single random distortion or severity can cause unstable and non-reproducible rankings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use multiple distortion types and severity levels and average across them.
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations

confounds.name: Temporal transition artifacts dominate detection
confounds.detail: Segment detectors may exploit obvious fake–real transitions rather than subtle fake content.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate on hand-crafted subsets with subtle transitions and report IoU/AUC there.
evidence: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos

confounds.name: Leaderboard overfitting or data leakage
confounds.detail: Tuning to validation/public test or leakage between train/test can inflate results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Hidden test evaluation with code submission and documented disjoint splits across datasets.
evidence: Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild

protocols.name: Corruption robustness sweep
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
protocols.detail: Evaluate on the same test set with multiple distortions (Gaussian blur, JPEG compression, additive noise, contrast and saturation/brightness changes) at several severity levels; report per-distortion AUC and the average over severities.

protocols.name: Aggregation choice disclosure
evidence: Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
protocols.detail: If ensembling or multi-view test-time augmentation is used, specify fusion rule (e.g., logit averaging) and views used (e.g., flips/rotations).

protocols.name: Cross-manipulation within FF++
evidence: DeepFake-Adapter: Dual-Level Adapter for DeepFake Detection
DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
protocols.detail: Train on one manipulation type or subset (e.g., DF/FS) and test on others (e.g., F2F/NT) to quantify manipulation-transfer performance.

protocols.name: Face preprocessing
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
protocols.detail: Detect and align faces (e.g., Dlib or RetinaFace), crop with a small margin, and resize faces to 256–384 px (typical: 256×256 or 300×300) before inference.

protocols.name: Pretraining declaration
evidence: DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
protocols.detail: State whether ImageNet (or other) pretraining is used for backbones and compare to random initialization where applicable.

protocols.name: Report efficiency alongside accuracy
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
protocols.detail: Measure parameter count, GFLOPs, and inference time per frame in addition to AUC/ACC.

protocols.name: Unified benchmark settings
evidence: DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
protocols.detail: Standardize preprocessing, frame sampling (e.g., 32 per video), optimizer (e.g., Adam lr=2e-4, batch=32), and evaluation metrics using a common framework (e.g., DeepfakeBench).

protocols.name: Held-out and hidden test evaluation
evidence: Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
protocols.detail: Use official challenge or benchmark splits with a public test and a hidden test set for final ranking to avoid overfitting to validation/public leaderboards.

protocols.name: Temporal fake-segment evaluation
evidence: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos
protocols.detail: For segment-level detection, compute IoU between predicted and ground-truth 1-D fake masks; optionally apply sliding-window smoothing and report both smoothed and unsmoothed results.

controls.name: Uniform retraining of baselines
evidence: DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
controls.detail: Re-implement or use official code to retrain all compared methods on the same training data/splits and preprocessing.
controls.rules_out: Performance differences arising from disparate training data, preprocessing, or initialization rather than the proposed intervention.

controls.name: Backbone and pretraining swaps
evidence: DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
controls.detail: Hold the pipeline fixed while changing backbones (e.g., ResNet/EfficientNet/Xception) and toggling ImageNet pretraining.
controls.rules_out: Improvements driven by backbone choice or pretraining rather than the proposed component.

controls.name: No-augmentation baseline and leave-one-out
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
controls.detail: Train the same model with no data augmentations and with all-but-one augmentations.
controls.rules_out: Gains attributable purely to augmentation pipelines instead of the proposed method.

controls.name: Single-model vs ensemble and fusion ablations
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
Process-Driven Modelling of Media Forensic Investigations-Considerations on the Example of DeepFake Detection
controls.detail: Report single-model performance and compare fusion strategies (majority vote, probability averaging, logit averaging).
controls.rules_out: Gains due solely to ensembling or a particular fusion operator.

controls.name: Chance (guessing) baseline
evidence: Process-Driven Modelling of Media Forensic Investigations-Considerations on the Example of DeepFake Detection
controls.detail: Include a random/guessing baseline or report kappa vs chance.
controls.rules_out: Detectors performing at chance level being mistaken for effective.

controls.name: Component ablations for adapters
evidence: DeepFake-Adapter: Dual-Level Adapter for DeepFake Detection
controls.detail: Remove individual adapter components (e.g., GBA-only, LSA-only) versus full adapter.
controls.rules_out: That a single submodule explains the full gain.

controls.name: Human-perception-vetted hard set
evidence: Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
controls.detail: Construct a hard test subset by retaining fakes judged real by humans in a blind study.
controls.rules_out: Evaluation hardness due to trivially visible artifacts rather than imperceptible forgeries.

controls.name: Inference-resolution and TTA ablations
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
controls.detail: Use the same checkpoint at different input resolutions and switch TTA (e.g., flips) on/off.
controls.rules_out: Apparent improvements caused by resolution scaling or test-time tricks rather than model design.

controls.name: Quality-level training variants
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
controls.detail: Train on FF++ Raw, c23, c40, and combined to test dependence on training compression level.
controls.rules_out: Apparent robustness due only to matching training compression to test conditions.

controls.name: Temporal modeling ablation
evidence: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos
controls.detail: Compare ViT-only frame classifier to ViT + temporal transformer; evaluate with and without smoothing.
controls.rules_out: Gains from temporal IoU/AUC caused by image encoder or post-hoc smoothing rather than temporal modeling.

controls.name: Uncompressed test baseline
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
controls.detail: Evaluate on pristine test data alongside distorted sets.
controls.rules_out: Robustness gains that come at the cost of clean-data accuracy.

controls.name: Within-domain-only vs cross-domain-only augmentation
evidence: Transcending Forgery Specificity with Latent Space Augmentation for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
controls.detail: Train with only within-domain augmentations and only cross-domain mixup in isolation.
controls.rules_out: Attribution of gains to one augmentation family when the other is responsible.

confounds.name: Overfitting to dataset/manipulation-specific artifacts

confounds.name: Gains due to augmentation choices or added synthetic data

DeepfakeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Deepfake Detection
Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
confounds.detail: Performance may improve from specific augmentations or extra synthetic data coverage rather than the proposed algorithm.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablations with/without augmentations, leave-one-out augmentation analyses, and retraining baselines on the same augmented data.

confounds.name: Inconsistent preprocessing/evaluation across methods

confounds.ruled_out_by: Robustness sweeps over blur/JPEG/noise/contrast/saturation and tests on GAN/diffusion-generated images; report per-distortion and average AUC.

Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Efficiency/practicality overlooked

Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection

confounds.name: Fusion operator artifacts
evidence: LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
Process-Driven Modelling of Media Forensic Investigations-Considerations on the Example of DeepFake Detection
confounds.detail: Performance differences could arise from a particular fusion rule rather than the added detectors/models.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare multiple fusion operators (e.g., majority, probability, logit averaging) and report consistent trends.

confounds.name: Leaderboard overfitting or data leakage
evidence: Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
LOGER: Local--Global Ensemble for Robust Deepfake Detection in the Wild
confounds.detail: Tuning to validation/public test or leakage between train/test can inflate results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Hidden test evaluation with code submission and documented disjoint splits across datasets.

confounds.name: Implementation/reimplementation errors
evidence: Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
confounds.detail: Discrepancies could be due to coding mistakes rather than true method differences.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Verify re-implementations against original reported results or use official code/weights where possible.

confounds.name: Temporal transition artifacts dominate detection
evidence: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos
confounds.detail: Segment detectors may exploit obvious fake–real transitions rather than subtle fake content.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate on hand-crafted subsets with subtle transitions and report IoU/AUC there.

confounds.name: Unstable rankings due to single random perturbation/severity
evidence: Assessment framework for deepfake detection in real-world situations
confounds.detail: Applying a single random distortion or severity can cause unstable and non-reproducible rankings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use multiple distortion types and severity levels and average across them.

confounds.name: Visual quality distribution differences drive performance
evidence: Inclusion 2024 Global Multimedia Deepfake Detection Challenge: Towards Multi-dimensional Face Forgery Detection
confounds.detail: Quality mismatches between real and fake (or between splits) may act as spurious cues.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Quantify quality distributions (e.g., CenseoQoE) and apply quality-degradation augmentations; validate on held-out and hidden tests.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using random uniform fake probabilities per frame aggregated to video-level scores, all three metrics must be near chance on FaceForensics++ (eval): 0.45 <= AUC <= 0.55 AND 0.45 <= Accuracy <= 0.55 AND 0.45 <= EER <= 0.55. Failure on any metric refutes evaluation correctness.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies the evaluation pipeline and metric computation are correctly implemented before any substantive testing.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train on FaceForensics++ (train) with standardized preprocessing (face detect+align, resize to 256–384 px) and video-level scoring via averaging 32 uniformly sampled frames per video. Validate on FaceForensics++ (eval) achieving AUC >= 0.90 AND EER <= 0.20; additionally, verify input crop size in [256,384] px and exactly 32 frames aggregated per video; face detection must succeed on >=95% of sampled frames. Any violation refutes apparatus readiness.
constraints_not_enforced: Exact FF++ compression level (c23 vs c40) if not specified by the source
experiment_recipes.rationale: Builds a standard, functioning baseline under a unified configuration, a prerequisite to test compliance with community norms.

experiment_recipes.goal: Cross-dataset eval on Celeb-DF complies with norms
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using the FF++-trained checkpoint (no fine-tuning on Celeb-DF), compute video-level AUC, EER, and AP on Celeb-DF (eval) with the same 32-frame aggregation. Pass if: (1) number of evaluated videos >= 1000; (2) AUC and EER are successfully computed (not NaN) with AUC >= 0.60; (3) training steps on Celeb-DF equal 0. Any failure refutes adherence to standard cross-dataset evaluation norms.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Confirms the standard cross-dataset generalization test (train on FF++, test on Celeb-DF) with prescribed video-level aggregation and metrics.

experiment_recipes.goal: Cross-dataset eval on DFDC Preview complies with norms
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using the same FF++-trained checkpoint, evaluate on DFDC Preview with 32-frame video scoring. Pass if: (1) number of evaluated videos >= 1000; (2) AUC and EER computed (not NaN) with AUC >= 0.60; (3) no DFDC Preview samples are used in training/fine-tuning (training steps on DFDC Preview = 0). Any failure refutes norm compliance.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Checks the widely used cross-dataset test on DFDC Preview, aligning with standard practice to assess generalization.

experiment_recipes.goal: Robustness sweep on Celeb-DF complies with norms
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On Celeb-DF (eval), run 5 distortion types (Gaussian blur, JPEG compression, additive Gaussian noise, contrast change, saturation/brightness change) each at 5 severity levels, plus clean (uncompressed) baseline, all with 32-frame aggregation. Pass if: (1) all 5 distortion families executed with exactly 5 severities each; (2) clean (undistorted) AUC is reported; (3) for each distortion, per-severity AUCs are computed and their mean per distortion is reported; (4) average AUC across all distortions and severities is computed; (5) clean AUC >= 0.55 to rule out broken setup. Any missing element refutes robustness reporting compliance.
constraints_not_enforced: Uncompressed raw-quality data availability if the source dataset lacks it
experiment_recipes.rationale: Evaluates and reports robustness across common corruptions and severities, a documented expectation to avoid overclaiming fragile detectors.

experiment_recipes.goal: Efficiency and ablations reporting complies with norms
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Measure and report Parameters (M) > 0, GFLOPs > 0, and Inference time per frame (ms) > 0 for the evaluated model at the used input size; additionally execute at least two attribution controls: (a) No-augmentation baseline and leave-one-out (report AUC), and (b) Backbone and pretraining swaps (swap to ResNet (baseline) or EfficientNet (baseline) with/without ImageNet pretraining; report AUC). Pass if all three efficiency metrics are positive and at least two attribution controls are executed with their AUCs reported. Failure to meet either criterion refutes compliance with standard control/efficiency reporting.
constraints_not_enforced: Single-model vs ensemble ablation if no ensembling is used
Exact hardware normalization for latency (reporting must include device spec externally)
depends_on: Cross-dataset eval on Celeb-DF complies with norms
Cross-dataset eval on DFDC Preview complies with norms
experiment_recipes.rationale: Prevents confounds by ensuring reported efficiency and basic attribution ablations (augmentations, backbone/pretraining) are present, aligning with common benchmarking practice.
